newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse edges up, market buoyant.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse edges up, market buoyant.

text.p: Blue-chips edged upwards at the Nairobi Stock Exchange on Tuesday, riding on buoyant market sentiment, bourse officials said.
The index gained 13.67 points to 3544.10. Turnover was posted at 21.0 million shillings traded on 396,628 shares compared to 1,509,453 shares on Monday.
Brokers said revived buying interest from foreign investors about three weeks ago had sparked this latest upswing.
"The market is good and looking very attractive," one broker said.

One broker speculated that the waiving of corporate gains tax levied on insurance companies for profits made on trading at the NSE -- effective January 1998 -- had given the bourse a new lease of life.
"Any bright people are going to buy (shares) now on the assumption that they'll be able to sell them off to insurance companies next year," he said.
Barclays Bank edged up three shilling to close at 113 while Standard Chartered Bank closed at 47.25 from 47. Kakuzi gained three shillings to close at 105 while Rea Vipingo closed at 9.60 from 9.30.
Kenya Power & Lighting closed at 175 from 171 while British American Tobacco, Kenya traded on the three-day special board at a reserve price of 61.50 from 61.
Foreign investors traded Kenya Commercial Bank at between 113 and 118 from 115 and National Industrial Bank at 60-61.50 from 60.
